claim: Antitrust plaintiffs satisfy the predominance requirement for class certification by using a damages model that estimates damages attributable to the antitrust injury on a class-wide basis, even if individualized determinations are later needed to allocate damages among class members.
initial_reasoning: In Re Bystolic Antitrust Litigation the court held that a damages model estimating class‑wide antitrust injury can satisfy Rule 23(b)(3) predominance, even though individual damage allocations may later be required. This directly supports the claim that such a model meets the predominance requirement for class certification.
